title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the table of contents (sections 38–46, MS pages 291–390) of the 'Deuxième partie : Variations sur l'équation des lacets'. It is the continuation of the 1981 manuscript 'La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois'. It contains no proofs, only section titles, so any reading of the mathematics is partly inference.

Notation, as best I can infer it:
- π_{0,3} = π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}), a free group on two generators; the hat denotes profinite completion.
- Γ = Γ_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q), acting by outer automorphisms on π̂_{0,3}.
- 𝔊_{0,3}, 𝔊^+_{0,3} (and 𝔆_{0,3}) are probably the cartographic and oriented cartographic groups of Longue Marche/Esquisse. The oriented one is ≅ Z/2 * Z and is closely tied to PSL(2,Z).
- π'_{0,3} is a distinguished subgroup or variant of π_{0,3}. Section 38 is the 'détermination' of an isomorphism π'_{0,3} ≅ 𝔊^+_{0,3}. Plausibly this makes explicit how π_1 of the thrice-punctured line sits relative to (P)SL(2,Z) and its commutator subgroup SL(2,Z)' (free of rank 2, index 12). The appearance of Sl(2,Z)' in sections 42 and 44 supports this.

The programme the titles outline:
- §39: congruence properties of the Γ_Q action on π_{0,3}. From these comes a homomorphism N_γ → GL(2,Ẑ), where N_γ is presumably a normaliser or stabiliser group attached to a loop γ.
- §40: a topological/isotopy paraphrase of the 'theory of loops' (lacets), i.e. a mapping-class/isotopy interpretation.
- §41: conditions for the isomorphism π̂'_{0,3} ≅ 𝔊̂^+_{0,3} to commute with outer Galois operations, and computation of the outer automorphism groups of π̂_{0,3} and of 𝔊̂^+_{0,3}.
- §42: recapitulation, in eight subsections: 𝔆_{0,3}; π_{0,3} and 𝔊_{0,3}; relations with π'_{0,3} and Sl(2,Z)'; automorphisms of 𝔊_{0,3}; automorphism–loop data for the profinite groups; cocycle computations in Sl(2,Ẑ)', including cocycles relative to σ_∞.
- §43: a digression on 1-cocycles of cyclic groups. Its parameters ρ, h, f, α, β play the role later played by Drinfeld's (λ, f) in GT, i.e. the 'loop equations' satisfied by the Galois image.
- §44: the equations transported into Sl(2,Ẑ).
- §45: a homomorphism M̃_{0,3} → G̃L(2,Ẑ)', and the construction of an extension Ñ of Γ by SL(2,Z)^. In modern terms this resembles 1 → SL(2,Z)^ → π_1(M_{1,1}/Q) → Γ_Q → 1, built here from genus-0 / three-point data.
- §46: 'definitive notations (?)' and a recapitulation.

The next page shows the sequel. It constructs a group scheme M_{ρ,σ} from the equation αρ(α)^{-1} = βσ(β)^{-1}ε_1(μ−1), together with a canonical map to GL(2) and homomorphisms from M̃_{0,3} into M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ). That suggests an attempt to algebraise the 'loop-equation' group as a group scheme over Z.
errors: No mathematical statements are proved on this page, so nothing can be checked. The notation (π' versus π, 𝔊 versus 𝔆, N_γ, M̃_{0,3}) is not defined here, and my identifications are tentative.
Page numbering is irregular (primed pages 307', 335', 336', 337'). The previous page notes that pages 291–292 appear twice.

ideas.what: Outer action of Γ_Q on π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) and its 'loop equations' with cocycle parameters (ρ, f, α, β, h)
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂, with Drinfeld's (λ, f) relations; Ihara's Galois representation on the profinite free group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Belyi (1979, injectivity); Ihara (1985–); Drinfeld (1990); Ihara (1991, GT)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and La Longue Marche (1981, circulated), in general form; the explicit equations of this second part are, as far as I know, unpublished

ideas.what: Congruence properties of the Galois action, giving a homomorphism N_γ → GL(2,Ẑ)
ideas.modern_name: Congruence-type properties of Galois/GT actions; images in GL(2,Ẑ) via abelianisation or elliptic-curve covers (Ihara's congruence results; Asada / Boggi congruence subgroup property)

ideas.what: Relation between π_{0,3}, the (oriented) cartographic group 𝔊^+_{0,3} and SL(2,Z)' (commutator subgroup, free of rank 2)
ideas.modern_name: Cartographic group / PSL(2,Z) and dessins d'enfants; punctured j=0 elliptic curve and SL(2,Z)'
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (cartographic groups); La Longue Marche

ideas.what: Construction of an extension of Γ by SL(2,Z)^ from three-point (genus-0) data
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic fundamental group of M_{1,1} over Q; GT̂ acting on SL(2,Z)^ and the genus-one Teichmüller tower
Mapping class group / braid interpretation of the Teichmüller tower

ideas.modern_name: Out of the profinite free group of rank 2 / Out(PSL(2,Z)^); anabelian rigidity

missed.claim: §45 constructs an extension of Γ by SL(2,Z)^ directly from genus-0, three-point data (M̃_{0,3} → G̃L(2,Ẑ)'). The sequel (§48) then constructs a group scheme M_{ρ,σ} receiving M̃_{0,3}, i.e. an algebraisation of the solution set of the loop equations. As far as I know, no group-scheme model of GT-type equations of this form appears in the literature. Pro-unipotent GRT/GT are the closest analogues, but they are not built this way.
missed.quote: L'hom. M_{0,3} → G̃l(2,Ẑ)', et construction de l'extension Ñ_γ de Γ par Sl(2,Z)^
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could give an independent, 1981 route to the genus-1 / SL(2,Z)^ arithmetic action. It might also give an integral group-scheme envelope of GT-type data, relevant to work on GT̂, SL(2,Z)^ and the genus-one tower (Lochak–Schneps, Enriquez's elliptic associators).

missed.claim: §39 announces 'congruence properties' of the Galois action on π_{0,3}, yielding a homomorphism to GL(2,Ẑ). This is an early precursor of later congruence results whose precise content is not recorded in published work.
missed.quote: Propriétés de congruence de l'opération de Γ_Q sur π_{0,3}, d'où l'hom. N_γ → Gl(2,Ẑ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may anticipate Ihara/Nakamura-type congruence statements. Comparing it with them would clarify priority.

deep.surprise_reason: This is only a table of contents, but it shows that in 1981 Grothendieck was explicitly working out (a) loop/cocycle equations for the Galois action on π̂_{0,3}, (b) a passage from three-point data to an extension of Γ_Q by SL(2,Z)^, and (c) a group-scheme algebraisation of those equations. Specialists know the general programme from Esquisse and Longue Marche, but the content of this 360-page second part is essentially unexplored. Without the actual pages, novelty cannot be confirmed.
transcription_corrections: §39: 'tirée :' is probably 'd'où :' or similar ('Propriétés de congruence … d'où l'hom. N_γ → Gl(2,Ẑ)').
§40: the line likely reads 'Paraphrase topologique-isotopique de la théorie des lacets' (no uncertainty marker needed).
§41: 'aux op. ext. de Γ_Q' means outer operations of Γ_Q; 'Calculs des autom. ext. des π̂_{0,3} et des 𝔊̂^+_{0,3}'.
Subsection I of §42 appears to be a calligraphic C (𝔆_{0,3}, likely the cartographic group), distinct from 𝔊_{0,3}.
§42.VII–VIII: the endings are hard to read. VIII is possibly 'cocycles sous σ_∞'.
§45: the extension symbol looks like 'Ñ' (possibly with tilde on γ or Γ), 'de Γ̃ par Sl(2,Z)^'. The final page number is 384 or 389.
Left margin note is rotated: 'NB les calculs de VII, VIII … [repris/rectifiés?] …', mostly illegible.
The final '2' is the page number of the table of contents.
